questions.q: Besides the virtual machine itself, what does a default az vm create command typically provision?
options: An OS disk, a network interface, and usually a public IP and network security group
Nothing else — it creates only the VM and nothing more
questions.explain: az vm create provisions a bundle of resources: the VM, its OS disk, a NIC, and by default a public IP and an NSG with a default admin-port rule.

questions.q: Which VM size family is burstable, with a baseline CPU level that can spend credits to burst higher for short periods?
questions.explain: B-series (Burstable) VMs accumulate CPU credits while idle and can spend them to burst above baseline, making them cost-effective for light, spiky workloads.

questions.q: A production application server needs steady, predictable CPU performance all day. Which size family best fits that need?
options: None of these — size family doesn't matter for production
questions.explain: D-series (general purpose) offers a balanced, consistent CPU-to-memory ratio with no bursting behavior, making it the default choice for steady production workloads.

questions.q: What does an image alias like Ubuntu2204 actually represent?
options: A random internal Azure ID with no public meaning
Shorthand for a full Marketplace URN in the form publisher:offer:sku:version
A custom image you must build yourself before first use
A VM size, not an image
questions.explain: Aliases like Ubuntu2204 are shorthand for a full Marketplace URN, e.g. Canonical:0001-com-ubuntu-server-jammy:22_04-lts-gen2:latest.

questions.q: Which VM size family is best suited to CPU-heavy batch processing or analytics jobs where memory isn't the bottleneck?
questions.explain: F-series (compute-optimized) provides a higher CPU-to-memory ratio than D-series, fitting workloads that need more raw CPU per core rather than more RAM.
